$comment: Benchmark corpus for the secure-me skill. `detect` cases contain a real vulnerability the skill must find. `control` cases look suspicious but are correctly written — reporting a finding on one is a false positive. See tests/README.md.

cases.expect: service_role key exposed to the browser through a NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment variable, bypassing row-level security
table holds per-user rows but row-level security is never enabled, so any authenticated client reads every row
security rules allow read and write to any authenticated user with no ownership check
token verified without pinning an algorithm, allowing alg:none and HMAC/RSA confusion to forge tokens
Server Action is a public endpoint but performs a privileged delete with no session or role check
handler fetches a record by client-supplied ID without verifying the caller owns it (BOLA/IDOR)
charge amount is taken from the request body instead of looked up server-side, letting a client set any price
webhook handler trusts the payload without verifying the Stripe signature, so anyone can forge payment events
user input concatenated into a SQL string instead of passed as a bound parameter
request body passed directly into a Mongo query, letting an attacker inject operators such as $ne to bypass the check
untrusted content rendered through dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no sanitization
server fetches a user-supplied URL with no allowlist, reachable to the cloud metadata endpoint for credential theft
origin is reflected back with credentials enabled, letting any site make authenticated cross-origin requests
passwords hashed with a fast unsalted digest instead of a memory-hard KDF
password reset token generated with Math.random, which is predictable and not a CSPRNG
untrusted fetched content is fed to an agent that can invoke a shell tool with no isolation or approval, enabling indirect prompt injection to command execution
an allowlisted column name is interpolated while all user values are bound parameters; this is correct and must not be reported as SQL injection
dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used with DOMPurify sanitization and a restrictive allowlist; this is correct and must not be reported as XSS
the Supabase anon key is publishable by design and is paired with row-level security; exposing it client-side is correct and must not be reported as a leaked secret
credentials are enabled but the origin is checked against a static allowlist; this is correct and must not be reported as a CORS misconfiguration
